source.title: Learning Multi-Level Features with Matryoshka SAEs

record.tranche_reason: The study measures first-letter feature splitting and absorption and finds markedly lower rates in Matryoshka SAEs than in BatchTopK SAEs, refining when these effects occur.
record.gate_note: The first-letter absorption and splitting evaluations and the Meta-SAE decoder-composition measurements bear on the claim. Reconstruction and downstream loss, concept-probing benchmarks, and automated interpretability results do not directly measure the claim's feature splitting or its proposed input partition and nearby directions, so they are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study compares Matryoshka and BatchTopK SAEs on Gemma-2-2B layer 8 with the first-letter absorption and splitting assays. It reports that a changed training objective sharply reduces both effects, which bears directly on V6, and also on V1, V2 and V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors say Matryoshka SAEs dramatically reduce absorption, splitting and composition and give cleaner concept separation, at a cost in reconstruction but with similar downstream loss. They call it a promising direction needing further validation.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses the first-letter task methodology for absorption and splitting, but compares standard BatchTopK SAEs with nested multi-objective Matryoshka SAEs. It trains on Gemma-2-2B layer 8 activations sampled from The Pile.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported absorption and splitting outcomes differ between Matryoshka and BatchTopK architectures. Absorption in BatchTopK increases with dictionary size; Matryoshka absorption stays around 0.03 as size increases.

fits_no_version.finding: Meta-SAEs explain substantially more variance in BatchTopK decoder directions than in Matryoshka decoder directions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Matryoshka training reduces shared or compositional structure among SAE decoder directions.

record.problems: The post reports only one trained Matryoshka SAE, on one model and layer. Absorption and splitting results are qualitative or approximate, with no per-size values or uncertainty estimates. The first-letter assay does not directly demonstrate that split latents partition the coarse feature's inputs or lie near its direction.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant rows were omitted. Reconstruction and downstream cross-entropy comparisons, other SAEBench metrics, and automated interpretability scores were excluded because they do not measure the claim's splitting, absorption, or cross-dictionary relationships.

untested.parts: Whether the split latents partition the coarse feature's inputs or lie near its direction, and the splitting rate per dictionary size.
Open SAE releases and models other than Gemma-2-2B layer 8.
Nested, geometrically close families that mirror a concept hierarchy.
Sparsity interventions within the standard objective, and a direct parent-hole versus child-firing analysis.
Decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents, and novel latents in larger SAEs.
Whether splitting reflects the model's own units, and isolating correlated or hierarchical inputs as the cause.

missing.what: Per-dictionary-size absorption and splitting values shown in the figures (the text gives only approximate endpoints).

record.verdict_notes: There is a single Matryoshka SAE, one model and one layer, and no uncertainty estimates. Splitting results are qualitative. The V1 and V2 limits_scope labels from Matryoshka overlap with the V6 support, because they rest on the same contrast.

versions.untested_parts: The first-letter task measures splitting across latents, but the post does not report whether those latents partition the coarse feature's inputs or lie near its direction.
The study tests Gemma-2-2B in one layer and compares two SAE architectures; it does not test open SAE releases or a range of large models.
No measurement tests whether split features form nested, geometrically close families or mirror a hierarchy in the model's representation.

The first-letter absorption assay does not directly test whether a parent fails to fire specifically where a child takes over. The study varies dictionary size but does not report a sparsity intervention intended to fix absorption.
The study does not compare larger-SAE latents with combinations of smaller-SAE latents or test whether larger SAEs add novel latents.

The study compares SAE architectures on a first-letter task, but does not directly establish that the effect says little about the model's own units or isolate correlated and hierarchical inputs as causes.

tranche.reason: The study uses a different objective (Matryoshka vs BatchTopK) with the first-letter assays. Its results bear on V6 and restate the scope of V1, V2 and V4. T3 or T2 would also be defensible.

source_check.notes: One Matryoshka SAE (five nested sub-SAEs, max 36864 latents, average L0 32), compared with five BatchTopK SAEs whose L0s (22-32) are matched to the sub-SAE sizes. Gemma-2-2B layer 8, 500M Pile tokens. Absorption values are approximate, with no per-size numbers; splitting is qualitative only. The states of r1 and r3 are V6 readings: for V4 (r1) and V1 (r3) the effect is near-absent under Matryoshka, as the verdict fixes say. The post shares an author with an original.

statements.correction: This study's V2 verdicts: supports for BatchTopK SAEs (r4); limits_scope for the Matryoshka SAE (l3, Gemma-2-2B layer 8).

statements.correction: r3: in the Matryoshka SAE (Gemma-2-2B layer 8, k-sparse probing on the first-letter task), first-letter features remain almost entirely unified. In BatchTopK SAEs they frequently split across multiple latents (r4). Absorption (~0.03 vs ~0.29) is a separate measure (r1, r2).
